generator.params.note: English ivy's climbing values (internode, shoot growth, clinging, seeking, draping, branching), with three stems from the foot for a twining vine. Changed from ivy: adult_rise 0 and adult_light 2, so no shoot takes ivy's upright adult habit (the honeysuckle has no such phase; it fruits on its free shoots once adult, as the climber did before revision 3); renew 0, as the deciduous grape's, so old nodes do not leaf again; max_shoot 2 for ivy's 3 and grown 8 years for ivy's 15, so the vine climbs to the 2 to 6 m (to 9 m) the model record gives rather than ivy's 16 m. Leaf card size, leaf life and fruit size now come from the traits by the vine form's rules; leaf_area and fruit_area are left to the form's defaults until the shading test gives this look's. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: About 5 m up its host at 8 years, within the model record's usual 2-6 m (record L2340188). Wide tolerance.

appearance.note: No source read gives the stem or leaf colour: a plain mid green and a grey-brown stem, by eye. The leaf is a plain simple blade whose outline and width follow the traits (ivy's lobed juvenile leaf dropped); berries round, coloured from fruit_colour_ripe.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: A twining woody vine (the model record: vine, woody, 2-6 m), drawn by the family's vine form on the climber program.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

host.note: The host it is grown on for rendering, the built-in ivy's 30-year bigleaf maple, a tree of the same Pacific Northwest woods; not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
